mergedParams.userDescription: Retro CRT monitor VHS static roll turn-off transition effects between videos

prompts.prompt: Create a retro CRT monitor turn-off transition preset that simulates the classic television shutdown effect. The transition should start with a horizontal collapse effect where the outgoing video compresses into a thin horizontal line (like old CRT monitors turning off), accompanied by a bright white flash. During the 0.8 second overlap period, add heavy VHS static noise overlay that rolls vertically. The incoming video should power on with a reverse effect - expanding from a horizontal line while the static gradually clears. Use a ShapeAtom to create the white phosphor line that appears during the collapse, and apply chromatic aberration filters to both videos during the transition for authentic analog distortion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with duration = video1.duration + video2.duration - 0.8s overlap. Outgoing VideoAtom: scaleY animation from 1 to 0.01 over 0.4s with ease-in-out-cubic, brightness filter spike to 200% at 0.2s. Incoming VideoAtom: starts at video1.duration - 0.8s, scaleY from 0.01 to 1 over 0.4s delay. Static overlay: VideoAtom with VHS static video loop, opacity 0 to 0.8 to 0 during overlap, mix-blend-mode: screen. ShapeAtom white line: height 2px, width 100%, opacity spike at turn-off moment. Both videos use filter effects with hue-rotate and blur for chromatic aberration. Z-index: outgoing=10, static=20, line=30, incoming=15.

prompts.prompt: Design a VHS tracking error transition that mimics the horizontal displacement and signal degradation when a VCR loses tracking. The transition should feature the outgoing video breaking into horizontal scan lines that shift left and right randomly (like tracking errors), while introducing RGB color channel separation. During the 1.2 second overlap, multiple displaced copies of the outgoing video should slide horizontally at different speeds, creating a 'torn signal' effect. The incoming video emerges through vertical rolling static bands that move upward, gradually stabilizing as the tracking 'locks in'. Include audio distortion effects that sync with the visual glitches.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with calculated duration, position: relative, overflow: hidden. Create 5 duplicate VideoAtoms of outgoing video with different translateX animations (-50px to 50px) using random timing, opacity 0.3 each, mix-blend-mode: screen. Main outgoing video: custom CSS filter for RGB split using drop-shadow. Rolling static: 3 ShapeAtoms with linear-gradient backgrounds, translateY animation from 100% to -100%, staggered timing. Incoming video: starts at -1.2s from end, initial transform: skewX(5deg), animates to skewX(0) over 0.8s. AudioAtom with distortion sound effect during transition. Provider mode effects targeting specific atoms via targetIds.

prompts.prompt: Build a retro static roll transition that simulates changing channels on an old television with vertical hold problems. The outgoing video should roll upward continuously while fading behind increasing static noise, creating the effect of losing vertical sync. During the 1.5 second overlap, implement a 'channel surf' effect with brief flashes of different colored static patterns (blue, green, magenta) representing different empty channels. The incoming video rolls down from the top while the static gradually decreases, eventually locking into place with a subtle magnetic 'snap' effect at the end.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with absolute positioned children, black background. Outgoing VideoAtom: translateY animation from 0 to -200% over 1.5s, linear easing, opacity 1 to 0.2. Static layers: 4 ImageAtoms with different static textures, opacity animations staggered, mix-blend-mode: exclusion. Channel flash effect: ShapeAtoms with solid colors, opacity spikes at 0.3s intervals. Incoming VideoAtom: initial translateY: 100%, animates to 0 over 1s with ease-out-back for 'snap' effect. Static noise AudioAtom with volume envelope matching visual static intensity. All animations use GPU-accelerated transforms.

prompts.prompt: Create a CRT phosphor burn-in transition where the outgoing video leaves a ghostly afterimage that slowly fades while the incoming video materializes. The effect should simulate the phosphor persistence of old monitors, with bright areas of the outgoing video lingering longer. Add horizontal scan lines that sweep across during the transition, and implement a degaussing effect where the image warps and color-shifts before settling. The 1.0 second overlap should feature a pulsing electromagnetic interference pattern that distorts both videos.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with duration calculation accounting for 1.0s overlap. Outgoing video: duplicate VideoAtom at lower z-index with brightness(2) contrast(0.5) filter for burn-in effect, slower fade out (1.5s vs 0.5s for main). Scan lines: ShapeAtom with repeating linear-gradient, translateY animation. Degaussing: both videos use transform rotate3d with sinusoidal animation, hue-rotate filter animation from 0 to 180deg to 0. EMI pattern: SVG-based ShapeAtom with radial gradient, scale pulsing animation, mix-blend-mode: color-dodge. Provider mode for synchronized effects across all atoms.

prompts.prompt: Design a VHS pause-glitch transition that recreates the distorted freeze frame when pausing a VCR. The outgoing video should freeze on the last frame, then distort with horizontal noise bands and color bleeding. During the 0.6 second transition, implement rapid frame jumping between the frozen outgoing frame and the first frame of incoming video, with increasing glitch artifacts. The incoming video should 'un-pause' with a characteristic VHS wobble and stabilization period. Add authentic VHS head-switching noise at the bottom of the frame.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Outgoing VideoAtom: endAt property to freeze last frame, custom CSS filters for distortion. Glitch bands: Multiple thin BaseLayouts with background gradients, random translateX animations, heights 2-5px. Frame jumping: Alternating opacity between outgoing (frozen) and incoming videos at 60ms intervals. Incoming video: initial transform scaleX(1.02) skewY(1deg), animates to normal over 0.4s. Head-switch noise: BaseLayout at bottom 10% with noise texture, opacity flicker. Short overlap (0.6s) for snappy transition. Z-ordering ensures proper layering of glitch elements.

prompts.prompt: Build a retro TV channel-change transition with authentic analog snow and signal acquisition. Start with the outgoing video deteriorating into diagonal rolling static lines, then transition through a period of pure white noise (snow) with occasional glimpses of the incoming signal trying to lock in. During the 2.0 second overlap, simulate the auto-tuning process with the incoming video fading in and out multiple times before finally stabilizing. Include the characteristic 'thunk' sound of channel changing and static audio that fades as the signal strengthens.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Complex timing with 2.0s overlap period. Outgoing: diagonal rolling via transform rotate(15deg) translateY animation, increasing blur filter. Snow effect: VideoAtom with white noise video, opacity 0.9, appears at 0.5s into transition. Incoming video: multiple opacity keyframes [0, 0.3, 0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.8, 1] over 1.5s to simulate signal acquisition. Rolling lines: Canvas-based ShapeAtom with animated diagonal stripes. Audio: Two AudioAtoms - channel change 'thunk' at start, static noise with fadeOut. BaseLayout duration = sum of videos - 2.0s overlap.

prompts.prompt: Create a CRT degaussing rainbow transition that simulates the colorful magnetic interference when degaussing an old monitor. The outgoing video should warp outward from the center with rainbow color bands rippling across it, while the screen briefly goes black. During the 1.3 second overlap, animated concentric rainbow circles should pulse from the center, with the incoming video gradually appearing through the interference. The effect should end with a satisfying 'snap' as the magnetic field normalizes and colors correct themselves.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Outgoing VideoAtom: scale animation from 1 to 1.5 with transform-origin center, combined with hue-rotate animation 0 to 720deg. Rainbow bands: Multiple ShapeAtoms with conic-gradient backgrounds, scale animations from 0 to 3, staggered timing. Black flash: BaseLayout with black background, z-index above outgoing, opacity spike. Incoming video: starts with saturate(0) filter, animates to saturate(1) over 0.8s, initial scale 0.8 to 1 with ease-out-back. Magnetic 'snap' via brightness filter spike at end. GPU-optimized with will-change: transform.

prompts.prompt: Design a VHS rewind glitch transition where the video appears to rapidly rewind with characteristic horizontal distortion bands. The outgoing video should accelerate backwards with increasing distortion, showing multiple 'ghost' frames overlapped. During the 0.9 second transition, create the effect of the tape mechanism catching and switching to play mode, with mechanical noise and temporary signal loss. The incoming video should start playing but with initial tape warble and gradually stabilizing tracking.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Outgoing VideoAtom with playbackRate: -3 for rewind effect, increasing blur filter over time. Ghost frames: 3 duplicate VideoAtoms with decreasing opacity (0.5, 0.3, 0.1) and translateX offsets. Distortion bands: AnimatedStripes component using CSS animations on pseudo-elements. Signal loss: Black BaseLayout with static noise texture, opacity 1 for 0.1s at midpoint. Incoming video: initial playbackRate: 0.95 ramping to 1.0, slight skewY transform for warble. Mechanical audio: AudioAtom with rewind sound effect. Timing: precise overlap at 0.9s for snappy mechanical feel.

prompts.prompt: Build a broken CRT screen transition that simulates a monitor with failing capacitors. The outgoing video should experience increasing vertical collapse, with the image compressing into bands that flicker and shift. During the 1.8 second overlap, implement random blackouts and geometry distortions as if the monitor is struggling to maintain the picture. The incoming video should appear in fragments, with different sections of the screen 'warming up' at different rates, eventually coalescing into a stable image. Add electrical buzzing and high-pitched whine audio effects.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Vertical collapse: Outgoing VideoAtom with scaleY animation incorporating step functions for flickering (steps(3)). Banding: Multiple masked sections using clip-path, each with independent opacity and translateY animations. Blackouts: Random opacity 0 keyframes at irregular intervals. Incoming video: Split into 4 quadrants using clip-path, each quadrant has delayed fade-in with different timing. Geometry distortion: perspective and rotateX transforms with sinusoidal animation. Audio: Two AudioAtoms - low frequency buzz (60Hz hum) and high frequency whine (15kHz), volume modulation matching visual glitches.

prompts.prompt: Create a retro broadcast signal interruption transition that mimics emergency broadcast system takeovers. The outgoing video should be abruptly cut by colored bars (SMPTE test pattern), followed by a brief 'no signal' blue screen. During the 1.1 second transition, show snippets of static interspersed with the incoming video trying to break through, as if switching between broadcasting stations. The incoming video should fade in with initial ghosting and double-image effects before the signal stabilizes. Include the iconic emergency broadcast tone during the color bars phase.
prompts.technicalSpecs: SMPTE bars: SVG ShapeAtom with precise color values (#FCFCFC, #FCFC00, etc.), appears instantly with z-index above outgoing. Blue screen: BaseLayout with RGB(0,0,255) background, appears after 0.3s. Signal interference: Rapidly alternating opacity between static texture, blue screen, and incoming video preview. Incoming VideoAtom: duplicate at 50% opacity with 5px translateX for ghosting effect, merges to single image over 0.5s. Emergency tone: AudioAtom with 1000Hz sine wave, 0.3s duration. Abrupt cut timing with stepped transitions rather than smooth easing.
